segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are testifying about yourself; your testimony is not true.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Even if I do testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet even if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone; it is I and the Father who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Even in your own law it is written that the testimony of two people is true.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where is your father?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spoke these words in the treasury, while teaching in the temple; and no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely he will not kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: That is why I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why am I speaking to you at all?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have many things to say about you and to judge. But the one who sent me is true, and what I heard from him is what I speak to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but speak these things just as the Father taught me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the one who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was saying these things, many believed in him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are Abraham’s offspring and have never been enslaved to anyone. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly I tell you, everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The slave does not remain in the household forever; the son remains forever.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will really be free.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know that you are Abraham’s offspring; yet you are seeking to kill me, because my word finds no room in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I speak of what I have seen with the Father; and you, then, do what you have heard from your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Our father is Abraham.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you are Abraham’s children, you would be doing the works of Abraham.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are doing the works of your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one father, God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If God were your father, you would love me, for I came from God and am here. I have not come on my own; he sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Why do you not understand what I am saying? Because you cannot hear my word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are from your father the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he tells a lie, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar and the father of lies.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Which of you convicts me of sin? If I am telling the truth, why do you not believe me?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is from God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you are not from God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I do not have a demon. I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it, and he judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly I tell you, anyone who keeps my word will never see death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet you say, ‘Anyone who keeps my word will never taste death.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Surely you are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who are you making yourself out to be?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say, ‘He is our God’;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet you have not come to know him. But I know him. If I said that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Your father Abraham was overjoyed that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly I tell you, before Abraham came to be, I am.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

notes.note: The story of the woman caught in adultery (7:53–8:11) is absent from the earliest manuscripts and appears at different places in later ones. The Greek edition translated here does not include it in the running text, so the chapter begins at verse 12 and continues the scene in the temple from chapter 7.

The setting is still the festival of Tabernacles (7:2, 37). The Mishnah describes great lamps lit in the temple’s Court of Women during that festival, and many interpreters think the saying plays on that ceremony, though John does not say so.

notes.phrase: the testimony of two people is true
notes.note: The reference is to the rule that a matter must be established by two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15; compare 17:6). In this legal context “true” carries the sense of valid or admissible, and some translations say “valid”. “True” is kept so that the reader can see the link with John’s wider language of truth.

The Greek is simply “I am” (egō eimi) with no complement, which is why the hearers ask “Who are you?” In ordinary Greek the phrase can mean “I am the one” or “it is I”, but it also echoes God’s self-declaration in the Greek version of Isaiah (for example 43:10, “that you may know and believe that I am he”). Some translations print “I AM” here and in verse 28 to bring out that echo; the same words are rendered “I am” in verse 58.

notes.phrase: Why am I speaking to you at all?
notes.traditional: Just what I have been telling you from the beginning
notes.note: This is one of the most obscure sentences in John, and the earliest manuscripts had no punctuation or word division to help. It can be read as an exasperated question, as here and in several ancient Greek commentators, or as a statement: “What I have been telling you from the beginning.” The Greek edition followed here punctuates it as a question; most English versions prefer the statement. The matter is unresolved.

The verb means both to raise physically and to exalt. John uses it for Jesus being raised on the cross (3:14; 12:32–33) with the second sense deliberately in play: the crucifixion is at the same time his exaltation.

The verb and the related noun in verses 34–35 refer to slavery, and the argument depends on the contrast between a slave and a free son of the household. Older versions used “bondage” and “servant”; most recent translations use “slave” in this passage.

The Greek has only “the father” in both halves, and the verb can be a statement (“you do”) or a command (“do”). On the reading adopted here Jesus is already contrasting his Father with theirs, as verses 41 and 44 make explicit. The alternative is an appeal: “so you too should do what you have heard from the Father.” Some manuscripts add “my” and “your” to settle the question.

“Fornication” is the traditional rendering, now obsolete and narrower than the Greek word; many modern versions paraphrase as “we are not illegitimate children”. The retort probably claims religious legitimacy, since the prophets picture unfaithfulness to God as sexual immorality. Some interpreters also hear an insinuation about Jesus’s own birth, but that is uncertain.

The argument since verse 38 turns on the idea that a person’s “father” is the one whose deeds that person does. The charge is made by a Jewish teacher against particular opponents whom he accuses of seeking his death, and comparable language for opponents appears in other Jewish writings of the period. The verse was later turned against Jews as a people, a use the context does not support.

The Greek says literally “a liar and the father of it” (or “of him”). The pronoun most naturally refers back to “the lie”, hence “father of lies”; it could also mean “father of the liar”. The reference to a murderer “from the beginning” is usually taken as an allusion to the serpent in Eden bringing death, or to Cain’s murder of Abel.

The Greek contrasts two verbs: Abraham “came to be”, while Jesus simply “is”, in the present tense. The absolute “I am” echoes God’s self-declarations in the Greek Scriptures (as in Isaiah 43:10 and Exodus 3:14). The attempt to stone him in the next verse shows that the hearers took it as a claim amounting to blasphemy.

candidates.reason: The double amen formula recurs 25 times in John and the single form throughout the Synoptics; renderings vary (truly, very truly, amen, I assure you) and should be fixed once.
A key Johannine word (abide/remain/stay/continue) whose thematic links across John and 1 John are lost if the English varies.
Translators alternate between witness and testimony, bear witness and testify; the legal theme runs through John, Acts and Revelation and needs one choice.
The absolute ἐγώ εἰμι recurs in John (4:26; 6:20; 13:19; 18:5–8) and in Mark, and needs a single policy on “I am”, “I am he” and “it is I”.
ἱερόν (the whole temple precinct) and ναός (the sanctuary building) are both traditionally “temple”; a consistent distinction, such as temple courts versus sanctuary, should be decided once.
